title: What is a zero-day, and why do they sell for millions?
description: A zero-day is a flaw attackers know about and the vendor doesn't. Here's why working exploits are worth so much, and how to shrink your risk.

scenes.big: Attackers found it before the vendor
scenes.say: A zero-day is a flaw that attackers know about, and the company behind the software doesn't.
It's called zero-day because the developer has had zero days to fix it. No patch exists yet, so even a fully updated device can be exposed.

lines: Your device says it's up to date
Attackers may already be using the flaw
scenes.say: Your phone says it's up to date. But a flaw the vendor has never heard of can't be fixed, so there's nothing to install.

So why the huge prices? A working exploit that quietly beats a fully patched phone is rare. Apple's public bounty tops out at two million dollars for the most advanced attack chains. Brokers have advertised similar sums.

steps: Install patches the day they land
scenes.say: You can't stop a zero-day, but you can shrink the window. Turn on automatic updates, and install patches the day they land. Follow for more threats, explained plainly.
